correctness.rationale: For Cr_n=K_n,n minus a fixed matching, independent zero sets have exactly three possible structures: empty, confined to one bipartition side, or the two endpoints of a single omitted matching edge. No-zero functions have weight at least 2n; two-sided zero case also at least 2n, with n(n−1)^2 equality assignments for the matching zero pair case when n=3. In one-sided-zero case the total domination of positive vertices on the fully positive opposite side requires at least two positive vertices on the zero side, while defense requires a two-label on the opposite side; minimum n+3, attained with two one-labels on zero side and a two-defender opposite at an index among those positive two. These equality conditions give 2n(n−1) for n>=4. For n=3, three disjoint tie cases contribute 1+12+12=25. Independent all-3^(2n) enumeration for n=3,4,5,6 yielded respectively (weight,count) (6,25),(7,24),(8,40),(9,60), including label shapes. The case-split proof establishes all n>=3.
residual_risks: Only exact minima and optimum counts are claimed; no enumeration of nonoptimal labelings or n=2.
